claims.text: Whether to close depends on location, time since injury, cause, contamination, and the patient's risk of infection or poor healing.
claims.quote: Deciding whether to close a wound (with suture or other methods of wound closure; eg, staples, skin adhesives) depends on the wound’s location, time since it occurred, cause, and degree of contamination and on patient risk factors for wound infection or poor wound healing.

claims.text: Primary closure usually suits clean wounds < 6 to 8 hours old (< 12 to 24 hours for face and scalp).
claims.quote: Primary closure is usually appropriate for uninfected and relatively uncontaminated wounds < 6 to 8 hours old ( < 12 to 24 hours for face and scalp wounds)

claims.text: Staples are quick and less likely than sutures to cause infection, but suit mainly straight cuts in low-tension areas, and not the face.
claims.quote: Staples are quick and easy to apply and, because there is minimal foreign material in the skin, are less likely to cause infection than sutures. However, they are suited mainly for straight, smooth cuts with perpendicular edges in areas of low skin tension. Improper wound edge apposition (sometimes causing wound edges to overlap) is the most common error. Staples should not be used on the face

claims.text: Skin adhesive is best for simple, regular lacerations, and not for wounds under tension unless the tension is relieved.
claims.quote: Adhesive is best for simple, regular lacerations; it should not be used for wounds under tension unless tension is relieved with deep dermal sutures, immobilization, or both.

claims.text: Adhesive strips are probably the quickest, with a very low infection rate, for wounds not under tension.
claims.quote: Adhesive strips are probably the quickest repair method and have a very low infection rate. They are useful for wounds not subject to tension.

claims.text: Sutures are best for irregular, heavily bleeding or complex lacerations, loose skin, areas under tension, and wounds needing deep dermal closure.
claims.quote: Sutures are the best choice for Irregular, heavily bleeding, or complex lacerations Areas of loose skin Areas under tension Wounds requiring deep dermal closure

claims.text: Sutures have the highest infection rate of the closure materials.
claims.quote: they have the highest rate of infection among materials used to close lacerations.
